role: Declares the nested Codable value types that make up AssistantContext (profile, session, workout history, baselines, trends, analysis summary, live workout and live HRV snapshots, route topology/weather/threshold/interval sub-snapshots). Pure data, no functions.
types: AssistantContext.WorkoutHistoryEntry: struct — per-workout compact metrics incl. power/cadence/alpha1/HRR/feeling
AssistantContext.SessionSnapshot: struct — full overnight session (score, factors, HRV domains, overnight HR, sleep, vitals, training, feeling)
AssistantContext.SessionSnapshotLite: struct — one-line recent session incl. ATL/CTL/TSB/ACWR and sleep stages

AssistantContext.ScoreFactorSnapshot / TimeDomainSnapshot / FrequencyDomainSnapshot / NonlinearSnapshot / ANSMetricsSnapshot / SleepSnapshot / VitalsSnapshot / TrainingSnapshot / BaselineSnapshot: structs — metric groups
AssistantContext.LiveWorkoutSnapshot: struct — live workout metrics, location, route, weather, trends, readiness, zones, predictions, thresholds, interval progress
AssistantContext.LiveWorkoutSnapshot.RouteTopologySnapshot / WeatherSnapshot / ThresholdSnapshot / IntervalProgressSnapshot: structs — live sub-snapshots
AssistantContext.LiveWorkoutSnapshot.RouteTopologySnapshot.ClimbSnapshot / TurnSnapshot: structs (extension) — climb and turn rows
toplevel: Only stored-property declarations with Codable synthesis. Defaulted vars on LiveWorkoutSnapshot (recognizedRouteWasAutoDetected=false, recentSplitGradeAdjustedPaces=[], historicalSportSampleCount=0, zone1..5Sec=0, activeThresholds=[], thresholdBreachSec=[:]) and RouteTopologySnapshot.turnsAhead=[] are defaults for memberwise init only: synthesized Decodable on a struct with a defaulted `var` still decodes the key with decode(), so they do not provide back-compat for payloads missing the key as the comments claim (LiveWorkoutSnapshot is Codable but no custom init(from:) exists here).

flags.text: SessionSnapshot.recoveryScore is commented '0-10 composite' while UserProfileSnapshot / AppKnowledgeBase describe the score as 0–100; renderers multiply by 10 (AssistantContext.swift:137,174,442). The 0-10 storage is real (RecoveryScoreCalculator+Composite.swift:64) so the comment is right but the scale split is a trap for any new renderer.

Non-optional vars with default values (recognizedRouteWasAutoDetected=false, recentSplitGradeAdjustedPaces=[], historicalSportSampleCount=0, zone1..5Sec=0, activeThresholds=[], thresholdBreachSec=[:], RouteTopologySnapshot.turnsAhead=[]) are commented as back-compat for older persisted sessions, but synthesized init(from:) decodes them with decode() and throws keyNotFound when absent. Latent: no code in the repo decodes these types (grep for LiveWorkoutSnapshot.self / AssistantContext.self finds nothing).
